speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, can you describe when these symptoms first started and if they have worsened over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing the "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness; to help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any difficulty with your speech, swallowing, or vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy).

The combination of subacute gait and limb ataxia in a patient with Crohn's disease on natalizumab is highly suggestive of PML, a severe opportunistic infection caused by the JC virus. I am requesting MRI images of the brain to confirm the presence of characteristic white matter lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI
